# UPDATE: WeRide Deep Dive

**From:** The AV Market Strategist <avmarketstrategist@substack.com>  
**Date:** 2026-08-25T07:04:40.000Z

---

👋 Hey everyone,
WeRide reported Q2 2026 on August 12. Two days later I sat down with Tony Han, WeRide’s co-founder and CEO, for a long conversation on Autonomy Insiders.
Between the two, enough moved that I went back into the living deep dive and rebuilt large parts of it. This is the biggest update I have made to any of these files.
If you have not come across them before: the deep dives are long-form company files I keep current, so that there is one document that is actually up to date instead of a pile of old posts. WeRide was the first. Pony.ai [ https://substack.com/redirect/f6acef50-03c1-4da9-ba58-6c8e690e9de5?j=eyJ1IjoiMXlnZjcifQ.KOUIeBfeCRzhIwFnKXyQigR4j0VpF-SZzascYhSZunw ] and the AV fleet operations layer [ https://substack.com/redirect/dc23d4ff-6c78-423c-9fb9-3864f83fc6e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMXlnZjcifQ.KOUIeBfeCRzhIwFnKXyQigR4j0VpF-SZzascYhSZunw ] followed. I update them whenever there is a material event.
What I changed this time
Q2 financials, rebuilt. Revenue, the record gross margin, operating expenses, and the loss. 
The unit economics section, rewritten from scratch. This is the change I spent the most time on. WeRide does not occupy the same position in every market, and I had been collapsing two different businesses into one set of numbers. Han corrected the same mistake publicly on the call. 
What WeRide earns per overseas robotaxi. For the first time, there is a disclosed figure. There are also two versions of it, given twenty-five minutes apart on the same call, and the gap between them matters.
A correction to my own runway math. I previously took the CFO’s burn rate and computed nine to twelve years of runway from it. The half-year balance sheet says I was too generous. The corrected number is in the file.
The quality of the loss. The headline improved. On the measure that matters, it did not, for the second reporting period running. The reason is worth understanding.
Fleet, footprint and permits, all current. Global L4 fleet, the robotaxi split, the Middle East doubling through a difficult quarter, three new European markets, and a year-end target that has been restated upward in a way that changes how to read it.
The regulatory moat, upgraded from my argument to their strategy. I have argued for a year that WeRide’s permit position is the most underappreciated thing about this company. In Q2 management made the same argument, in stronger terms than I had used. They also named the condition under which it stops working, which is the part nobody quoted.
New: the foundation models. WITT and GENESIS, what they do, and the strategic claim underneath them that justifies WeRide’s entire three-segment structure. Including why the model is named after a German philosopher.
New: where WeRide goes next. Han named an expansion pipeline rather than a signed deployment, which he has not done publicly before. One of the countries on that list surprised me.
The Uber concentration risk, updated. I flagged this as a prospective risk. It is no longer prospective. An analyst put it to management directly on the call, and the answer was a good one. It was also not an answer to the question that was asked.
From the podcast. What WeRide deliberately refuses to build and why. How breakeven differs between China, the Gulf and Europe, with the definition management actually uses. And a deployment criterion Han named that I have not heard another AV executive state.
The weekly newsletter is free, and it stays free.
The deep dives are the part I keep for the readers who chose to support this work when they did not have to. If you are on the free list, this is exactly what a paid subscription funds.
If you already support The AV Market Strategist, thank you. The updated file is live now, and the conversation with Tony Han is here: Autonomy Insiders EP24 [ https://substack.com/redirect/e7fe17ab-7773-4ed2-9653-225b71403406?j=eyJ1IjoiMXlnZjcifQ.KOUIeBfeCRzhIwFnKXyQigR4j0VpF-SZzascYhSZunw ].
Thanks for reading.
Daniel
